name: devkit-for-strapi-mcp

tools.name: server_info
tools.description: The running DevKit server: its version (the one to name in a bug report), the licence tier, which tools really run (without a licence the Pro tools answer an upsell), the indexed roots and how current the index is (`freshness`).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the Strapi projects discovered in the workspace (name, root, Strapi version, counts, `freshness`). Call this first in a multi-project workspace, then pass `from`/`project` to the other tools; project_info gives one project in full.

tools.name: project_info
tools.description: One project in full: Strapi version, TS or JS, package manager, API prefix, counts, every local and installed plugin with whether DevKit verifies refs into it (and if not, why), health and freshness. Call it to orient yourself, or when a plugin ref comes back `external`.

from.description: A path inside the project (the file you are editing; relative to its root with `project`), in a multi-project workspace.

project.description: A project name or root, when no path is at hand.

tools.name: add_project
tools.description: Index a Strapi project from an ABSOLUTE path: its root or any file/folder inside it (a folder is also scanned downward, for monorepos). Use it when a tool returns `noProject`. Idempotent; returns the projects now known.

path.description: Absolute path to the Strapi project root, or to any file/folder inside it.

tools.name: refresh
tools.description: Rescan every project from disk and rebuild the index. Rarely needed: each call already re-indexes what changed on disk. For a project added since startup, or edits made outside on a project whose `freshness.diskTracking` is 'off'.

cold.description: Also read every installed plugin again, ignoring the cache (slower; default false).

tools.name: config_sync_diff
tools.description: The diff config-sync's admin page shows, from the real plugin: each entry that differs between config/sync and the database (`different`, `only-in-db`, `only-in-sync-dir`, `invalid-file`: not JSON, empty or not an object), what differs in a few words, and its `likelyDirection` (import | export | unknown) from the file's git history. It includes what a Strapi start changes by itself: after changing a schema, a controller or a route, export those entries and commit them with the code. It loads the project's Strapi the way config-sync's CLI does, which writes to the database as a `strapi develop` start does (schema sync, migrations): a local development database only — a remote one, or a Strapi 4 database under Strapi 5 code, is refused first. A few seconds.

tools.name: config_sync_export
tools.description: Write entries from the database into config/sync with the plugin's own export, in the exact form config-sync compares. Only entries that differ; one only in config/sync has its file deleted; an `invalid-file` is replaced only when named. Commit the files with the code that caused them. It loads the project's Strapi the way config-sync's CLI does, which writes to the database as a `strapi develop` start does (schema sync, migrations): a local development database only — a remote one, or a Strapi 4 database under Strapi 5 code, is refused first.

tools.name: config_sync_import
tools.description: Apply config/sync entries to the database with the plugin's own import (a role, a content-manager view, a setting). `keys` is required, never everything; an entry only in the database is deleted from it; an `invalid-file` is never imported. The entries still different afterwards are exported back (`reexport`), so the diff converges. Refused with NODE_ENV=production. It loads the project's Strapi the way config-sync's CLI does, which writes to the database as a `strapi develop` start does (schema sync, migrations): a local development database only — a remote one, or a Strapi 4 database under Strapi 5 code, is refused first.

instructions:
DevKit for Strapi knows the real UIDs, services, controllers, policies, middlewares, routes and schemas of the Strapi projects in this workspace, read statically (Strapi is not started — except by the Pro config_sync_diff/export/import tools, which load it when called).
1. Orient: list_projects (several projects → pass `from`, a path inside the one you work on, to every tool); project_info for one project in full.
2. Before writing a magic string (UID, service/controller ref, route handler, policy), call validate_reference: `unknown` comes with didYouMean; `external` means the plugin can't be verified (project_info says why). Never invent a UID.
3. Read the real shape: get_schema for fields, list_routes for routes, find_references / dependents before changing something.
4. Refactor in two steps: a plan_* tool (dry-run) → review → apply_edits with its planId; then list_broken_refs should return nothing.
5. When a project uses config-sync (project_info.configSync): config_sync_status lists its files. Prefer an export (the admin Config Sync page, `npx config-sync export`) to editing config/sync/*.json by hand: config-sync compares each file as written with the database.
6. With Pro, config-sync through the project's own Strapi: config_sync_diff gives the real diff (what a start changes included). After changing a schema, a controller or a route: config_sync_diff, then config_sync_export the entries your change caused, and commit them with the code. To change a role or a content-manager view: edit its file, config_sync_import it (the plugin then writes it back in its own form). A DevKit rename or move also updates the config/sync files it concerns, unless `configSync: false` is passed or the user turned it off (strapiDevkit.configSync.followRefactors): its warnings say which files it updated, or left with the old names. Importing them is the user's call — the local database is shared by every branch; config_sync_import loads Strapi with the new code.
Answers reflect the files on disk: what changed outside this session is re-indexed before each call (unless a project's freshness.diskTracking is 'off' — then call refresh). File paths in an answer are relative to its `root`. server_info says which tools need a Pro licence.
